No rule in the KrishiLoop database specifies an imidacloprid dose for brown planthopper in rice. The available rules (e.g., R-BDR-001, R-BDR-002, R-BDR-003) only define counting thresholds and advise contacting your officer for control options when thresholds are exceeded. They do not provide any pesticide amounts, concentrations, or brand names.
No rule found for tomato bacterial wilt in Kenya. The current rule packs only cover rice and potato diseases.
The KrishiLoop rules do not specify any mancozeb dosage, nor any fungicide dose per knapsack sprayer, for potato late blight. Therefore I cannot provide a grams-per-15-litre recommendation.
Since the brown planthopper count exceeds the threshold, you should contact your agricultural officer immediately for control options. Do not spray without consulting them.

When humid, mild days are forecast and your potato crop is not protected against late blight, the rule advises you to contact your agricultural officer immediately about protection options. This guidance comes from the CIP technical manual on potato late blight.
During booting, heading, or flowering, inspect the base of the panicle (the neck) for brown spots, which indicate neck blast. If you find such spots, report them to your agricultural officer.
The available rules for brown planthopper in rice do not specify a dose for imidacloprid per litre of water. Therefore, I cannot provide a pesticide dose from the sourced rules.
